annotations.title: Who is the greater.
annotations.text: The occasion of this question and of their contention for Superioritie among the rest of their infirmities which they had before the comming of the Holy Ghost, was (as certaine holy Doctors write) vpon emulation toward Peter, whom only they saw preferred before the rest in the payment of the tribute, ◦by these wordes of our Sauiour, Geue it them for me and thee. Chrys. ho. 59. Hiero. in Mat. Vpon this place.

annotations.title: Scandals.
annotations.text: The simple be most annoyed by taking scandal of their preachers, Priests, and elders il life: and great damnation is to the guides of the people whether they be temporal or spiritual, but specially to the spiritual, if by their il example and slaunderous life the people be scandalized.

annotations.title: Hand, foote, eye.
annotations.text: By these partes of the body so necessarie and profitable for a man, is signified, that whatsoeuer is neerest and deerest to vs, wife, children, freendes, riches, al are to be contemned and forsaken for to saue our soule.

annotations.title: Their Angels.
annotations.text: ◦ A great dignitie and a maruelous benefite that euery one hath from his Natiuitie an Angel for his custodie and Patronage against the wicked before the face of God. Hiero. vpon this place. And the thing is so plaine, that Caluin dare not deny it, and yet he wil needes doubt of it, lib. 1. Inst. c. 14. sect. 7.

annotations.title: Not heare the Church.
annotations.text: [1] Not only Heretikes, but any other obstinate offender that wil not be iudged nor ruled by the Church, may be excommunicated, and so made as an Heathen or Publican was to the Iewes, by the discipline of the same, casting him out of the felowship of Catholikes. Which [2] Excommunication is a greater punishement then if he were executed by sword, fire, and wild beastes. Aug. cont. Adu. leg. li. 1. c. 17. And againe he saith, Man is more sharply and pitefully bound by the Churches Keies, then with any yron or adamantine manicles or fetters in the world. August. ibidem.

annotations.title: Heathen.
annotations.text: Heretikes therfore because they wil not heare the Church, be no better nor no otherwise to be esteemed of Catholikes, then heathen men and Publicans were esteemed among the Iewes.

annotations.title: You shal binde.
annotations.text: [1] As before he gaue this power of binding and loosing ouer the whole, first of al and principally to Peter, vpon whom he builded his Church: so here not only to Peter, [2]and in him to his successors, but also to the other Apostles, and in them to their successors, euery one in their charge. Hieron. lib. 1. c. 14. aduers. Iouin. and Epist. ad Heliod. Cyprian. de Vnit. Eccl. nu. 3.

annotations.title: Shal loose.
annotations.text: Our Lord geueth no lesse right and authoritie to the Churche to loose, then to binde, as S. Ambrose <mn>◦</mn> writeth against the Nouatians, who confessed that the Priests had power to binde, but not to loose.

annotations.title: In the middes of them.
annotations.text: ◦ Not al assemblies may chalenge the presence of Christ, but only such as be gathered together in the vnity of the Church. and therfore no conuenticles of Heretikes directly gathering against the Churche, are warranted by this place. Cypr. de vnit. Eccles. nu. 7. 8.

annotations.title: Seuentie times seuen.
annotations.text: There must be no end of forgeuing them that be penitent, either in the Sacrament by absolution, or one man an other their offenses.
